articles.title: McGraw Hill CEO Philip Moyer Overviews Its First Investor Day since 2025 IPO
articles.summary: How is one of the world's leading education companies using artificial intelligence, curriculum innovation, and digital learning to reshape the future of education? Following McGraw Hill's Investor Day at the New York Stock Exchange, Phillip Moyer, CEO of McGraw Hill, joined Kristen Scholer to discuss the company's growth strategy, leadership position in educational content, AI roadmap, K-12 opportunities, higher education momentum, and long-term financial outlook. A major theme throughout the conversation is the size and importance of the global education market. Moyer notes that education represents a multi-trillion-dollar industry and remains one of the most significant areas for long-term innovation and investment. The interview also explores McGraw Hill's leadership position in higher education. The company continues to expand market share through digital delivery, affordable access initiatives, curriculum innovation, and strong educator relationships. Another key topic is sustained momentum in the higher education segment. Moyer highlights the company's multi-year streak of market share gains and attributes that growth to product innovation, customer service, and broad institutional adoption. The conversation further examines Inclusive Access, a model that provides students with access to educational materials as part of tuition or course fees, helping improve affordability and day-one access to course content. A significant focus of the discussion is McGraw Hill's Evergreen content strategy. The company continuously updates instructional content, assessments, and educational resources, allowing instructors to maintain current course materials more efficiently. The interview also highlights the organization's strong position in K-12 education. Another major theme is literacy. McGraw Hill has invested heavily in programs aligned with the Science of Reading, an evidence-based approach to literacy instruction that is gaining broader adoption across U.S. schools. The discussion explores changing educational standards and increasing demand for curriculum solutions that support reading proficiency, literacy improvement, teacher development, and dyslexia screening. Additionally, Moyer discusses challenges facing educators, including teacher burnout and the need for more effective instructional tools and support systems. The conversation further examines the role of artificial intelligence in education. Another key topic is trust. Moyer argues that educational AI systems must be grounded in high-quality instructional content, safety standards, and demonstrated effectiveness rather than relying solely on general-purpose AI models. The interview also highlights McGraw Hill's efforts to integrate AI directly into educational workflows while maintaining educator oversight and classroom relevance. A significant focus is the company's agentic AI strategy. Rather than simply answering questions, AI agents can help support learning objectives, deliver contextual assistance, and provide personalized educational experiences. The discussion further explores how AI-powered learning systems may accompany students throughout their educational and professional journeys. Another important theme is lifelong learning. Moyer envisions educational content becoming increasingly adaptable and accessible across academic, professional, and continuing education environments. The interview also examines opportunities within healthcare education, where AI-powered tools may help medical students and professionals access relevant educational information more efficiently. A significant focus is McGraw Hill's financial profile. During Investor Day, the company outlined expectations for continued cash flow generation and long-term shareholder value creation. The discussion further explores management's confidence in both operating performance and future growth opportunities across higher education, K-12 instruction, professional learning, and AI-enabled educational services. Another key theme is innovation. Moyer emphasizes that McGraw Hill's long history, trusted brand, educator relationships, and content assets position the company to remain a leader during the next phase of educational transformation. Looking ahead, McGraw Hill expects to continue investing in AI-powered learning tools, literacy programs, digital curriculum delivery, higher education solutions, educator support, and lifelong learning experiences. Throughout the discussion, Moyer shares insights on education technology, artificial intelligence, digital learning, literacy instruction, higher education, K-12 curriculum, lifelong learning, agentic AI, educational innovation, and shareholder value creation.
